title: Grade 8 Math — Mon, Jun 16
description: Playing with Numbers — Day 1 of 5: General form of numbers; reversing digits
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A 2-digit number has tens digit 'a' and units digit 'b'. Its general form is:
questions.explanation: A 2-digit number with tens digit a and units digit b = 10 × a + b = 10a + b. Example: 37 = 10(3) + 7.

questions.question: A 3-digit number has hundreds digit 'a', tens digit 'b', units digit 'c'. Its general form is:
The number 43 in general form is:
questions.explanation: 43 has tens digit 4 and units digit 3. General form = 10 × 4 + 3 = 40 + 3 = 43.

questions.question: If a 2-digit number is 'ab' (tens digit a, units digit b), what is the number formed by reversing its digits?
questions.explanation: Reversing ab gives ba. General form of ba = 10b + a.

questions.question: A 2-digit number is 73. If we reverse its digits we get 37. What is the sum of these two numbers?
A 2-digit number is 73. If we reverse its digits we get 37. What is the difference (73 − 37)?
The difference between a 2-digit number and its reverse is always divisible by:
questions.explanation: (10a + b) − (10b + a) = 9(a − b). The difference is always divisible by 9.

questions.question: The sum of a 2-digit number and its reverse is always divisible by:
questions.explanation: (10a + b) + (10b + a) = 11(a + b). The sum is always divisible by 11.

questions.question: A 3-digit number 325 has its digits reversed to form 523. What is 523 − 325?
If a number has digits 'a' and 'b' with a > b, which is larger: the original (ab) or reversed (ba)?
questions.explanation: If a > b, then 10a + b > 10b + a (since 9a > 9b → 9(a − b) > 0). The original ab is larger.

questions.question: Express 97 using its general form (10a + b) and identify a and b.
questions.explanation: 97 has tens digit 9 (= a) and units digit 7 (= b). So 10(9) + 7 = 90 + 7 = 97. ✓

A number with digits a and b (10a + b) when added to the number with digits reversed (10b + a) gives 143. What is a + b?
Why do we write numbers in 'general form' (10a + b) in mathematics?
options: To prove divisibility rules and number puzzles using algebra
questions.explanation: Writing numbers in general form allows us to use algebraic manipulation to prove divisibility rules and solve number puzzles.
